entry.Applicability: A kc-dev-flow-2 change whose goal is to cut what First Officer (FO) reads, such as moving rule text out of the adopted README (references/sd/workflow.md) into a mod, a script's printed output or another file, where acceptance is stated as a word count.
entry.Evidence: In task fo-lifecycle-mod (iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins#643, closure revision d2c1d80085b2699e4cad79eecd4c13fe2230647d) the first design's criterion AC-2 bounded only references/sd/workflow.md words (5561 down to 5483); validation recommended PASSED at that design, yet FO then measured FO's total reading as up by about 507 words while the README shrank by 80, and the Captain sent the task back (amendment 3). The redo counted words FO reads per moment, and the landed mod cut that total from 2036 to 1699 with every moment lower. Recorded in spacedock-state/dev2:_archive/fo-lifecycle-mod.md under '### Why the cycle-2 design grew' and '### Words FO reads at each moment', and in the Cycle 1 FO line of its feedback record. Checked 2026-10-15: git grep for a per-moment reading count over ab9334edf03d3f248bd8e28a6be979307f355f36 finds only the per-file budget in lint-skills.py; no project rule, selected-profile text or stage principle states this practice.
entry.Practice: State the acceptance number as the words FO reads at each lifecycle moment (startup, idle on an open PR, idle on a merged PR, after the archive, the merge ask): every passage and every script output that instructs a step due at that moment, counted the same way for the unchanged base and for the candidate, with each moment required to fall below its base. Do not accept the size of the one file the text left (for example WORKFLOW_WORD_BUDGET in kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py) as the measure, because that number can fall while FO's total reading rises. Bounded: one task; the redesign also gave each step one home, so the count is not shown to be the only cause of the reduction; the recount script lives only in the archived task's validation folder, not in the repository; and a validator found the first recount script under-counted one moment, so recount with an independent copy.

evidence: Route: filed after an observer read of a relay FO session that never ran pr_watch and archived a merged task with no observer report or learn, because it read the README only to line 480. First design (README rules plus two mod files restating them) passed validation, then the Captain sent it back (amendment 3) when FO measured that FO's total reading grew by about 507 words while the README shrank by 80. The redo (one home per step, scripts print the next action, STE writing rules and review-finding rules of amendment 4) reduced reading at every moment. Codex rounds 3 to 6 each left a P1 about pr_watch.py deciding the merge ask; FO stopped the loop under the circuit-breaker rule and the Captain narrowed the scope (amendment 6): the script reports facts and the merge-ask decision stays with FO and delivery_gate.py. Round 7 P1 (directory-form tasks) fixed; round 8 no P1. Replays: S2 met the observer-before-sentinel and learn-after-archive steps; S1 one design run met the loop, one stopped at the engage prompt like the control.

Delivery: iamcxa/kc-claude-plugins#643 squash-merged 2026-10-14T23:25:55Z as ab9334edf03d3f248bd8e28a6be979307f355f36 from head 3a3cfc30bba2687127cd480913577135c4bfa4e7 (one 48-word Spacedock mod runs pr_watch.py tasks at startup and idle; scripts print the next step for recording a PR, keeping one wait, the observer before the sentinel and learn after the archive; pr_watch.py reports facts and does not decide the merge ask; ADR 0015; workflow.md 5581 to 5511; words FO reads per moment 2036 to 1699).
decisions.reason: Existing rules cover one home per step and counts as diagnostics, but none says which quantity to count when the goal is reader load; the per-file budget passed a first design whose total reading grew, and the per-moment count is what exposed it and bounded the redo. One task is one case, not proof of general effectiveness.

The observer's violations (missing alignment Result line, Supersedes: none on amendments 3 and 6, bare script names in dispatch records, declines without reasons) are each already stated in the project's docs/dev2/README.md (Captain amendments, Stages, Review-finding disposition) and the ideation principles; a rule not followed is no-change, not a new entry.

The acceptance run that picked up an older spacedock binary on a minimal PATH is covered by the validation principles: the acceptance script names any install it needs and runs unchanged in a fresh shell.

Codex rounds 3 to 6 repeating the pr_watch.py merge-ask P1 and FO stopping under the circuit-breaker with a Captain scope narrowing is covered by the README review-finding rules (P1 blocks, round 3 declines non-P1) and the Captain's authority over scope; no project condition beyond them is shown.

Workers stopping on a sonnet weekly usage limit and stream stalls are environment events with no practice change or avoided error attributed. The existing git config entry already covers the repository-config ban restated in this dispatch.
